hardware_families.label: ACME modular hardware in the CIR
hardware_families.quote: The six experiments in the ACME project featured flames of gaseous fuels and were all conducted with the same modular set of ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).

hardware_families.label: Droplet apparatus (MDCA) in the CIR
hardware_families.quote: FLEX, FLEX-2, and the Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) each featured burning droplets of liquid fuel and were conducted with the Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the CIR.

hardware_families.label: Glovebox (MSG) flow duct
hardware_families.quote: BASS, BASS-II, the Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE), and the Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE) collectively featured both solid and gaseous fuels. Each of these investigations was conducted within the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) using the modular fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE.

hardware_families.label: Saffire in a Cygnus cargo vehicle

notes.quote: One of the instruments used for smoke detection in the SAME and SAME-R studies was instead used to detect dust in the Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT and DAFT-2) studies.

Partial gravity was mimicked in ACME's Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (E-FIELD Flames) experiment through the effect of the electric field on the ions that naturally occur in flames.

Microgravity tests with the highest oxygen concentrations were conducted as part of the ACME's Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G). In those tests, the combustion chamber was filled with a mixture of nitrogen and a flammable gas (e.g., propane), while an oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen flowed from the spherical burner creating an inside-out flame.
